sourceDecisionQuestions.question: Goterón/vierteaguas names the drip edge; archived larmier is plausible but regional trade usage needs confirmation. Rake/borde de hastial becomes rive latérale du toit, which may cover a broader edge. Resolve term senses together with dictionary entries.
Alero/eave is the lower roof edge; archived avant-toit may mean the entire overhang. Select a precise French trade term for the installation point under this plan.

Sub-capa/fieltro and underlayment may name different materials across roof systems. Archived sous-couche is generic; choose the source and product-specific dictionary sense before scoring the under/over question.

The source card says install drip edge first, while the Reader asks under versus over underlayment and requires checking manufacturer instructions; the Reader 6 eave command is explicitly according to the plan. Do not promote an unconditional construction sequence without qualified roof-system and plan review.
Cutting drip edge at the corner is this source scene's instruction, not a general cut detail. Confirm the actual approved product and corner detail before a scored imperative or audio script.

The source speaking ask is to have the installer explain the approved sequence; archived speaking adds a request to show manufacturer instructions. Keep the extra ask as domain evidence and maintain the exact source objective in scored modes until reviewed.
